text.p: Base metals had varying degrees of success on Tuesday in recovering from Monday's fund-led sell off, with copper and zinc making the best progress.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau Index ended 0.48 points lower at 239.98

Buoyed by a stock drawdown and trade interest, benchmark three months LME copper climbed $14 to finish the afternoon kerb at $2,292 per tonne. But the lower prices were not enough to lure long-awaited Chinese buying, a physical trader said. Chartwise, copper still looked vulnerable and may have to head still lower before posting further advances, analysts said. Zinc similarly climbed $13 to finish at $1,260, after tumbling $20 on Monday.

Aluminium dipped initially, with stocks showing a rise of 2,675 tonnes after Monday's inventory decline. But for most of the day it consolidated in a tight range, with limited trade buying failing to lift prices above a high of $1,588. It ended virtually unchanged at $1,582.50, down $0.50.
Lead prices hovered just above the $650 level and ended the kerb $3 firmer at $653. A trader noted that lead saw good buying at Monday's lows, in which consumers covered about half of their needs.
Nickel edged barely higher to $7,305, up $15, while tin climbed $20, to $5,740.
Alloy was quiet but was last indicated weaker at $1,470/$1,474, versus $1,485.

CBOT wheat futures closed higher on renewed concerns about weather problems in portions of the U.S. crop, export hopes and on a strong rally in KCBT wheat futures, traders said. The Kansas City market rallied on a decline in the amount of deliverable-grade wheat in Kansas City elevators, KCBT traders said. Wheat futures closed 1-1/2 to four cents per bushel higher, with May up 1-1/2 at $3.82.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly higher Tuesday, but volume remained low and historical volatilities continued to drift back in most of the complex. "Neither volume, nor volatility nor lease rates have responded much lately, despite whispers of more central bank gold sales, or the jump in the dollar again today," Chase Manhattan New York managing director Dinsa Mehta said. COMEX June gold ended up $0.20 at $351.20 an ounce after trading from $350.50 to $352.30, within the range of $348.30 to $358.00 during the past month.

NYMEX gasoline prices ended higher Tuesday on the back of firm cash values in the U.S. Gulf while gasoline demand gathered pace abroad. "Gasoline in the (U.S.) Gulf and Midcontinent have risen while there are plenty of stories about Nigeria needing gasoline," said Warren Tashnek, president of Fimat USA Futures in Houston. May gasoline settled up 0.45 cent a gallon at 61.17 cents. May heating oil ended off 0.23 cent a gallon at 52.89 cents while May crude finished up 12 cents a barrel at $19.35.
